acceptance_criteria.text: The release inventory and acceptance evidence contain functioning deliverables for all four areas and both reasoning modes; a roadmap, design, mockup, or disconnected prototype does not replace any required capability.
Optional installation or activation of a backend means a configurable delivered feature, not permission to omit its implementation or acceptance.

requirements.assessment: All four required areas and both reasoning modes have working source and installed interfaces, with actual backend, model, native and browser evidence joined in the integrated acceptance report.
requirements.title: Deliver all second-release capabilities

acceptance_criteria.text: Existing valid records and core commands remain compatible; added semantic profiles and fields have explicit versions and capabilities, and unsupported older readers fail clearly rather than misinterpret them.
No automatic memory or Task schema migration, concept-ID recycling, core-ID redefinition, or child-project adoption occurs.
Acceptance of integration requires evidence that the applicable first-release foundation works; the first TRD's trd_done status alone does not prove implementation.

requirements.assessment: Core v1 commands run with site packages disabled; exact core and historical-state hashes are preserved. Wrapper version2 is explicit and rejected by unsupported readers. No automatic product adoption or canonical memory/Task migration occurred.
requirements.title: Preserve the first-release foundation

acceptance_criteria.text: Core lookup, validation, and wiki generation operate with all advanced profiles absent or disabled; enabled advanced operations report missing or incompatible dependencies without claiming success.
Installation, model preparation, service startup, and profile upgrades occur only through separately selected setup operations; a query or document approval performs none of them.

Profiles report their exact runtime/package/model versions and input compatibility; RDFLib and pySHACL remain the report-derived standards-backend basis, with exact versions selected and tested during planning.

requirements.assessment: Separate exact package/model runtimes were explicitly prepared. Core-only and disabled cases do not provision dependencies; unavailable enabled profiles report non-success. Root readiness distinguishes selection, installation and validation.
requirements.title: Isolate and explicitly provision optional backends

acceptance_criteria.text: Remote JSON-LD contexts, unselected OWL imports, escaping paths, symlinks, external XML resources, and federated query targets cannot cause unauthorized reads or network requests.
Uploaded ontology content cannot enable executable extensions, plugins, JavaScript, Python code, or custom query functions; supported extensions are explicitly registered project capabilities.
Tests observe prohibited access attempts being blocked, rather than relying only on a denylist of literal strings or a documentation warning.

requirements.assessment: Actual confined worker probes observe network/file/process denial. Parsed context/import/XML/query/extension policies reject unselected access, with canonical preservation checks rather than string-denylist-only evidence.
requirements.title: Restrict untrusted ontology input

acceptance_criteria.text: The adapter exposes separately identifiable graph contexts for the included fact classes and records exact canonical inputs, module versions, configuration, and adapter version.
Materializing or querying the RDF projection does not make it an alternative authoring store or change canonical ontology bytes.
Only selected, permitted project modules and bindings enter the dataset; a cross-system link does not import another project's graph automatically.

requirements.assessment: The RDF adapter distinguishes asserted, inferred, derived and external graph contexts, carries exact project/module/source versions and preserves canonical bytes. Dataset selection does not import linked projects.
requirements.title: Provide an RDF dataset projection

acceptance_criteria.text: Export followed by staged re-import preserves the supported identities, typed values, relations, and graph membership; semantic equivalence accounts for serialization order and blank-node renaming.

A graph-only export identifies its selected graph and supplies a companion context/provenance manifest or explicitly rejects an unsupported lossless export; it never silently flattens distinct fact classes.
Imported data is validated and staged as an attributed proposal, with namespace conflicts and unsupported constructs reported before any canonical publication.
Export destinations and overwrite behavior are explicit; imports cannot overwrite canonical content or grant trust merely because their syntax is valid.

requirements.assessment: Actual JSON-LD/Turtle/RDF-XML staging and dataset manifests preserve graph identity, typed/language literals and blank-node semantic equivalence. Unsupported lossless conversions and conflicting imports fail without canonical publication.
requirements.title: Import and export without silent semantic loss

acceptance_criteria.text: A result can be traced to the exact source entity and the activity that produced it; available producer attribution and derivation links survive export.
Provenance identifies evidence and production history, not execution permission or approval of a proposal.
Changed or missing evidence is visible as stale or unavailable rather than represented as verified current provenance.

requirements.assessment: PROV-O entities, source/activity attribution and derivation links survive selected interchange. Freshness checks expose changed sources and provide no authority; final provenance and negative-assertion cases extend the original report.
requirements.title: Expose standards-compatible provenance

acceptance_criteria.text: Representative queries return tabular bindings, a Boolean answer, or a result graph as appropriate, with project/dataset identity, versions, and whether asserted or inferred graphs were selected.
Named-graph selection is explicit; graph-producing queries return results without inserting them into canonical or persistent stores.
Supported DESCRIBE behavior, result ordering, and nondeterministic expressions are documented; repeatability checks use a defined deterministic query/result profile.

requirements.assessment: Actual SELECT, ASK, CONSTRUCT and DESCRIBE cases run over selected local named graphs and return versioned result forms. Graph output is transient; deterministic restrictions and DESCRIBE scope are documented.
requirements.title: Provide read-only SPARQL queries

acceptance_criteria.text: Update operations and SERVICE federation are rejected; FROM and FROM NAMED can select only already permitted local dataset graphs and cannot trigger retrieval of external resources.
Malformed, prohibited, cancelled, or resource-limited queries return distinct diagnostics; partial results are not labeled complete.
Query execution changes no canonical or generated persistent state, and cannot silently install a backend or refresh an index.

requirements.assessment: Actual update, SERVICE and disallowed FROM cases are rejected. Cancellation, invalid syntax and bounded execution retain distinct non-success states. Snapshot and timestamp checks show queries do not build persistent state.
requirements.title: Prevent query mutation and uncontrolled expansion

acceptance_criteria.text: Shapes cover required definitions/provenance, identity references, relation endpoint types, and configured cardinalities; overlap with core checks yields compatible results.
Reports distinguish conformance, violations, and inability to complete validation, and identify the affected entity, path, shape, severity, and useful diagnostic.
Invalid shapes, unsupported features, missing backends, and processing errors cannot become a passing validation or an execution authorization.
Validation identifies its graph scope and whether inference was applied; inferred triples cannot supply missing approval/provenance or bypass the core authoring checks.

requirements.assessment: Actual pySHACL cases test valid and invalid graphs, compatible core checks, definitions, endpoints, provenance/cardinality, invalid/unsupported shapes and incomplete results. Inference cannot supply authoring approval.
requirements.title: Validate graph constraints with SHACL

acceptance_criteria.text: Approved rules and example facts yield the expected additional types or relationships, including a generated wiki page being recognized as an Artifact through its declared type hierarchy.
The supported reasoning profile and its limits are explicit; required competency cases determine profile adequacy, and unsupported axioms are reported rather than silently ignored.
Draft proposals and merely similar labels do not enter the approved reasoning premises; identity equivalence requires an approved semantic assertion.

requirements.assessment: The finite rule engine derives the generated wiki Artifact type and declared property conclusions, with an independent owlrl oracle for supported examples. Drafts and lexical similarity are excluded from premises; unsupported axioms are explicit.
requirements.title: Derive facts from approved ontology rules

acceptance_criteria.text: An agent and a human can distinguish authored assertions, inferred conclusions, and AI suggestions and inspect the premise/rule chain for a selected inferred result.
Rebuilding or discarding inference results changes no canonical assertion or historical memory; accepting a proposed semantic change still requires publication.
A reasoning pass never grants Task, role, tool, or publication authority.

requirements.assessment: Assertions, derived proofs and suggestions retain separate fact/source types in APIs and the browser. Selected proofs expose exact premises and rules; neither recomputation nor a reasoning result publishes assertions or grants authority.
requirements.title: Explain and separate inferred results

acceptance_criteria.text: An absent relationship is not automatically treated as false or as a permission denial/approval unless an explicit applicable constraint defines that interpretation.
Inconsistent approved premises produce an actionable conflict report; unrelated conclusions are not presented as trustworthy merely because the engine completed.
Validation and authorization decisions use their own explicit rules rather than treating incomplete inference as proof of compliance.

requirements.assessment: Actual unproven, explicit-negative, inconsistent and unsupported cases retain their distinct outcomes. A conflicting closure is untrusted, and explicit validation/authorization remains independent.
requirements.title: Report uncertainty and contradiction accurately

acceptance_criteria.text: Limit exhaustion, cancellation, unsupported semantics, and stale input return clear non-success states; no incomplete closure is silently labeled complete.
Identical pinned inputs produce equivalent conclusions and stable normalized evidence; changing a premise invalidates dependent results.
Live recomputation does not replace the ontology packet already frozen for an active solver round.

requirements.assessment: Actual finite budgets/cancellation and stale-input cases fail truthfully; pinned repeat runs preserve normalized proofs. Frozen solver packets remain immutable when live approved facts change.
requirements.title: Bound and reproduce reasoning runs

acceptance_criteria.text: An authorized agent/model run produces a concrete structured proposal from an identified source packet, with supporting references, rationale, affected identities, and explicit uncertainty.
Instructions embedded in sources remain data; generated content cannot expand read/write scope, invoke actions, or approve itself.
Generation uses an explicitly permitted runtime and source scope; it does not silently provision a model, request credentials, or send project data to a new service.

requirements.assessment: Two actual native generation runs used exact permitted source packets and captured structured candidates. The embedded source instruction did not become a candidate instruction or expand the permitted output; source/runtime gates were separately tested.
requirements.title: Generate ontology proposals from permitted evidence

acceptance_criteria.text: A proposal displays its evidence, semantic diff, generator attribution, current review state, and any superseding revision; unsupported claims are visible.
Revising or regenerating a proposal preserves its earlier review history and invalidates approvals tied to obsolete content.
AI generation need not be byte-deterministic; review, validation, and publication bind the exact captured candidate bytes.

requirements.assessment: Durable revisions retain exact bytes, generator attribution, semantic diff and superseded review history. Browser inspection showed actual native request/result attribution, with model/effort names explicitly unobserved rather than invented.
requirements.title: Keep proposals attributable and reviewable

acceptance_criteria.text: Candidate checks run without publishing the proposal or contaminating approved retrieval; reports identify regressions, conflicts, unsupported semantics, and source freshness.
A candidate cannot become eligible merely because an LLM endorses it or because it passes syntax validation.
Reviewers can inspect the affected definitions, relations, generated wiki/query results, and downstream semantic effects before accepting exact content.

requirements.assessment: Real candidate validation runs core, SHACL, competency and formal-impact checks in an isolated overlay. Unsupported or malformed candidates cannot become eligible, and review exposes affected records and downstream changes.
requirements.title: Validate proposals before publication

acceptance_criteria.text: Approval binds the exact current proposal and target hashes; stale evidence, changed targets, missing grants, or conflicting ownership prevent publication.
Accept, reject, revise, and supersede have distinct recorded outcomes; rejecting or discarding a proposal changes no approved ontology.
An approved edit becomes canonical only when its actual publication receipt and reopened target bytes establish success; partial failure reports its real committed boundary.

requirements.assessment: Exact grant, source and target hashes are checked by the existing publisher. Actual native and browser publication receipts were reopened; stale/rejected/partial cases preserve their true committed boundary and durable recovery state.
requirements.title: Publish only approved exact proposals

acceptance_criteria.text: A revised proposal addresses named findings and retains source/version lineage; unchanged failures or exhausted limits stop with unresolved findings.
Evaluation shows whether the candidate improves the relevant competency behavior and reports regressions or lack of benefit without requiring a predetermined improvement percentage.
Training or self-modification of the agent is not required to perform this proposal-refinement workflow.

requirements.assessment: The second native candidate addressed a named stale-target finding while preserving concurrent work and source lineage. Bounded revision tests stop repeated failures and retain neutral/negative evaluation outcomes.
requirements.title: Refine proposals using observed feedback

acceptance_criteria.text: With the profile enabled, an otherwise missed paraphrase can return a sourced ontology concept labeled as a semantic match; it does not displace an exact identity match.
Model/index/input versions and stale-index status are visible; absence of the profile preserves first-release lexical and graph retrieval.
Embedding similarity does not establish semantic equivalence, approve a new concept, or access sources excluded from the selected project or frozen packet.

requirements.assessment: The actual local embedding model recovered a missed paraphrase and retained exact-identity priority. Model/index/helper/source versions and freshness are explicit. Frozen search uses captured vectors only; similarity grants no equivalence or authority.
requirements.title: Add optional ontology semantic retrieval

acceptance_criteria.text: The comparison records the dataset, ontology/configuration/model versions, expected facts and sources, retrieval correctness, attribution, resource use, and observed failures.
An automatically extracted graph remains exploratory or proposed knowledge; it is not promoted to normative project vocabulary by the evaluation.
The report's published study percentages are not treated as guaranteed Sys4AI outcomes; useful negative or neutral results remain valid evidence.

requirements.assessment: The reproducible comparison records exact corpus/config/model versions, sources, expectations, time/resource observations and false positives. Root top5 correctness was3/6 lexical and5/6 semantic, while top1 stayed3/6; no promised study percentage is adopted.
requirements.title: Evaluate graph-assisted reasoning and retrieval

acceptance_criteria.text: Coverage includes applicable ontology and memory publication, Task lifecycle/ownership operations, TRD/plan lifecycle operations, role/asset changes, and project setup/adoption through their supported project interfaces.
Every covered operation resolves to a current action contract and dispatch binding; missing, stale, and unsupported bindings are reported explicitly.
Action contracts describe semantic validity and capability; current user/role/Task authority still determines whether the actor may act.

requirements.assessment: Every declared consequential helper operation is bound to an exact contract. The REVIEW-001 correction adds real target/input/lifecycle/capability semantics while retaining the current owner authorizer as a separate gate.
requirements.title: Define semantic contracts for governed actions

acceptance_criteria.text: A semantically invalid covered request reaches no underlying mutation helper; a valid request proceeds only after the existing authorization checks succeed.
Guarding is demonstrated through actual dispatch adapters, not only an independently callable validator that callers may accidentally omit.

Coverage diagnostics distinguish guarded project paths from direct host/third-party paths outside the integration; the system makes no unsupported claim of intercepting every native tool or shell command.

requirements.assessment: Real owning dispatch adapters validate structure, run enabled semantics, then retain owner authorization and execution. Natural invalid requests prove that the continuation is not invoked. Coverage explicitly excludes arbitrary shell and third-party paths.
requirements.title: Enforce guards in the execution path

acceptance_criteria.text: Each failure returns its action identity, failing condition, relevant source/version, and an actionable diagnostic without invoking the requested side effect.
A timeout, unknown result, or backend failure cannot be converted to a pass, and retry does not silently disable the guard.
An explicitly disabled guard profile is reported as disabled; existing authorization checks remain active and no disabled path is advertised as semantically protected.

requirements.assessment: Enabled guards reject invalid or ambiguous inputs, unsupported contracts, stale state and backend failure. Failure diagnostics retain action/context evidence and an actionable condition; retry cannot silently disable the guard.
requirements.title: Fail closed when an enabled guard cannot validate

acceptance_criteria.text: Changing arguments, a target revision, an ontology rule, governing source, manager generation, or approval scope invalidates the old decision.
Tests exercise a change between preview/check and dispatch; a stale pass cannot authorize the new operation.
The integration respects existing helper transactions and locks, reports real consistency limits, and does not fabricate a cross-system atomicity guarantee.

requirements.assessment: Decision hashes bind exact requests, targets, sources, role/Task context and selected contracts. Actual changes inside each family's existing lock reject stale decisions. No cross-system atomicity is claimed.
requirements.title: Bind a guard decision to the exact operation

acceptance_criteria.text: A successful record identifies the checked request, decision versions, authoritative authorization outcome, actual helper receipt, and verified target result.
Semantic success without authorization or execution is reported only as semantic success; errors and partial mutations retain their true status.
Logs and durable receipts contain bounded operational evidence without credentials, unnecessary personal data, hidden reasoning, or full transcripts.

requirements.assessment: Successful guard receipts link the semantic check, exact request/context, owner result and reopened state. Independent authorization and partial-failure receipts remain distinct; observations contain bounded evidence, not hidden reasoning or credentials.
requirements.title: Record guard outcomes and verify effects

acceptance_criteria.text: A user can find a concept by ID, label, or alias; inspect incoming/outgoing relations; filter by module, type, lifecycle, or fact classification; and navigate to its source evidence.
Approved assertions, inferred facts, imported material, and AI proposals remain visually distinguishable, with a readable list/inspector alternative to the graph.
The workbench reports the selected project and current readiness accurately and does not require a hosted website or remote service for basic browsing.

requirements.assessment: The actual root and fixture browsers displayed project/readiness identity, ID/label/alias search, filters, typed relations and source navigation, with separate assertion/inference/proposal labels and a non-graph inspector.
requirements.title: Provide a local ontology workbench

acceptance_criteria.text: An author can add a concept and relationship, edit their supported fields, validate the draft, and inspect the resulting semantic diff without hand-editing JSON.
Imported locked core content is protected; project extensions and distinct replacement identities follow existing rules rather than silently redefining an imported ID.
Deprecation/replacement preserves historical IDs, while unsupported destructive changes are rejected or routed through their separately authorized lifecycle.

requirements.assessment: Actual browser forms created and revised a sourced project instance; real service tests create composite concepts/relations, reject invalid endpoints and preserve deprecation/replacement history. Locked core edits are denied.
requirements.title: Support real visual authoring

acceptance_criteria.text: A user can inspect an AI proposal's evidence and validation results, revise or reject it, and publish only when the actual current project authority permits the exact operation.
Draft saving, successful validation, and clicking a review control do not themselves approve or publish canonical semantics.
After publication, the workbench reopens the canonical result and shows its real status and receipt; it does not declare success from a queued request alone.

requirements.assessment: The browser inspected actual native proposal attribution, reviewed an exact diff, rejected/reopened a candidate, and published only through a current trusted-author session and normal guarded publisher. Receipt and canonical result were reopened.
requirements.title: Connect visual review to governed publication

acceptance_criteria.text: Two clients editing the same target cannot silently overwrite each other; a stale save or publish reports the conflict and retains the draft for review.
Cancel, discard, and failed validation leave approved content unchanged; a partial publication shows exactly what committed and what remains unresolved.
Reloading or reopening a saved draft preserves its identity, content, evidence, and review state.

requirements.assessment: Two actual browser tabs produced a rejected stale save with the pending text retained. Reload preserved proposal/review identity; invalid/rejected drafts and partial publisher tests leave canonical data at the truthful pre/post boundary.
requirements.title: Preserve edits during conflicts and failures

acceptance_criteria.text: A user can complete search, draft editing, validation, diff review, and the permitted publication/rejection flow without relying on graph dragging or color alone.
Field errors identify what failed and preserve entered content; loading, unavailable profiles, stale results, and partial failures have distinct visible states.
The main flow explains concepts and review consequences without exposing unnecessary implementation details.

requirements.assessment: Keyboard search and form/review controls completed the non-graph workflow. Field/validation errors retained input; actual narrow500px content had no horizontal overflow. No390px browser run is claimed.
requirements.title: Make workbench actions understandable and accessible

acceptance_criteria.text: The default listener is restricted to the local machine; remotely exposing it requires a separate selected deployment and access policy.

Forged actor fields, stale review tokens, unauthorized browser origins/requests, escaping file paths, and executable content in labels/imports do not cause unauthorized reads, writes, or script execution.
Browser controls use the same guarded publication/validation interfaces as other supported clients and retain their exact target/version checks.

requirements.assessment: The service binds loopback and checks Host, Origin, CSRF, current actor and exact targets. Actual HTTP negatives reject forged authority and escaping sources; an actual browser renders an executable-looking label as literal text without an image or script execution.
requirements.title: Protect local editor and query endpoints

acceptance_criteria.text: The current manager freezes exact packet bytes before dispatch and supplies identical references to every independent initial solver, including queued solvers.
Further queries cannot add live facts, new AI proposals, new embeddings/documents, changed rules, or sibling/current-execution candidate material outside the permitted frozen inputs.
The packet uses existing path/SHA256 interfaces and size limits; selection/truncation is explicit and no new Task schema field or ownership route is introduced.

requirements.assessment: Actual independent initial native solvers received identical frozen version2 packet/baseline digests before any sibling candidate was imported. Captured scope and existing Task path/hash bounds remain intact, including separately tested frozen semantic vectors.
requirements.title: Freeze advanced ontology context

acceptance_criteria.text: A newly published concept or rule does not silently enter active solver context; the manager assesses its effect and repeats the existing affected input/review/acceptance gates when material.
Execution guards check current approved action context and reject an action based on stale inputs without rewriting the solver's frozen packet.
Ontology integration neither replaces the current Task manager nor changes required team composition, role authority, or lifecycle status.

requirements.assessment: The actual confirmed manager published a scoped late fact after initial forks, recorded materiality, reconciled solvers and delivered same-ID revised input handoffs before followup dispatch. Initial packet bytes stayed unchanged; current guard checks remain separate.
requirements.title: Reassess material advanced-context changes

acceptance_criteria.text: Ontology inference, proposal publication, visual editing, and RDF import/export do not rewrite existing memory records or add unsupported fields.
Advanced mixed queries retain the identities and source types of definitions, inferences, proposals, and historical evidence and cannot upgrade memory into operational authority.
Memory-side mutations occur only through their own authorized operations; new semantic links remain derived and versioned.

requirements.assessment: Exact root memory hashes remain unchanged. Actual advanced mixed retrieval retains ontology, historical_memory, ontology_inference and ontology_proposal identities/source types without promoting history or drafts to authority.
requirements.title: Preserve memory history and retrieval scope

acceptance_criteria.text: The root installation exposes and verifies all four capability areas against current root bindings, with exact versions and readiness for the selected profiles.
Reusable assets contain no root project instances, proposal history, credentials, generated indexes, or runtime state.
Adoption preserves unrelated local files and existing approvals/authority; any needed governance-binding refresh is exact, scoped, and verified rather than inferred from file similarity.

requirements.assessment: Exact source/root adoption receipts and final package/Template comparisons bind the installed capability. Neutral reusable assets contain no root records or prepared runtime state. Root-local Task intake policy is preserved as an explicit merge exception.
requirements.title: Deliver reusable sources and root integration

acceptance_criteria.text: New/first-prepared projects receive their own identity, locked core/extension versions, and empty project data; backend/model activation and publication authority are destination-local and accurately reported.
Existing projects and prior receipt editions retain their content, configuration, imports, licenses, memory choices, and provenance until an exact adoption/upgrade is selected.
Customized or incompatible packages are preserved and diagnosed; upgrades and recovery use current expected versions and the existing receipt model, with no bulk product propagation.

requirements.assessment: Installed v9 initializer cases cover distinct new/first-prepared identities, neutral profile selections, populated prior-edition adoption, customized-package rejection and exact interrupted recovery. Original receipts, memory choices and licensing remain preserved.
requirements.title: Extend neutral setup and selected upgrades

acceptance_criteria.text: A maintainer can enable an authorized profile, run inference/SPARQL/SHACL, generate and review a proposal, visually edit a draft, and understand a rejected action using the delivered instructions.
Captured drafts/proposals, approvals, and publication/recovery receipts remain durable; rebuilding graphs or indexes cannot delete that accepted work.
Documentation and health output distinguish implemented, installed, enabled, validated, guarded, and unexercised capabilities, and report limitations without advertising unsupported behavior.

requirements.assessment: Installed/source command and verification guides document setup, inference/query/validation, proposal generation/review/publication, browser use and guard recovery. Durable proposals/receipts are kept separate from rebuildable graphs and indexes, and capability states are reported explicitly.
requirements.title: Document operational contracts and durable state

acceptance_criteria.text: Tests cover graph/dataset round trips, typed/language-tagged literals, source/provenance retention, all supported query forms, shape conformance, violations, and validation failure.
Tests observe rejection of SPARQL updates, SERVICE, remote contexts/imports, external XML resources, escaping paths, untrusted executable extensions, and resource-limit violations.
Actual results identify dependency/profile/input versions; successful core-only tests or mocked backend outputs cannot prove this requirement.

requirements.assessment: The real pinned backend test suite observes all supported query forms, typed/language/provenance round trips, conformance/violations/failure, parser access restrictions and actual worker resource controls. Synthetic validator outputs are not the acceptance basis.
requirements.title: Verify standards interoperability and access controls

acceptance_criteria.text: Cases show a correct inferred type and property relationship with inspectable premises/rules, an unproven conclusion that remains unproven, and an inconsistent or unsupported case that does not pass as valid.
Changing an approved premise invalidates its dependent result; a bounded/cancelled run reports incomplete reasoning accurately.
Captured outputs prove engine behavior and versioned evidence rather than relying on an LLM's prose explanation of what the engine should do.

requirements.assessment: Actual rule-engine evidence includes type and property conclusions, premise/rule inspection, unproven/contradictory/unsupported outcomes, stale-premise rejection and incomplete bounded/cancelled runs, checked with current source tests.
requirements.title: Verify actual formal inference

acceptance_criteria.text: An actual authorized model/agent run generates a sourced candidate; a supported change can be reviewed and published through the normal gate, while unsupported or conflicting content remains unapproved.
Evaluation includes changed evidence, stale approval, attempted instruction injection, and a revision responding to a concrete validation finding.
Prewritten candidates or parser tests alone do not establish proposal-generation capability; missing runtime evidence remains explicitly unverified.

requirements.assessment: Actual native candidates, an observed named-finding revision and reopened governed publication establish generation acceptance. Changed evidence, stale review and source-instruction boundaries are retained separately from parser/fixture tests.
requirements.title: Verify AI generation and governed acceptance

acceptance_criteria.text: The coverage report maps each supported action family and dispatch path to observed tests; negative cases prove that the underlying side effect was not invoked.
At least one valid authorized action reaches its owning helper and its result is reopened; semantic success without authority is rejected.
Input changes between preview and execution invalidate the earlier pass, and execution/partial failure receipts retain truthful status.
Any uncovered host or direct bypass path is disclosed as outside observed coverage rather than described as protected.

requirements.assessment: The corrected current dispatch matrix combines real backend natural-negative cases with valid owner actions and reopened results, per-boundary coverage, under-lock changes and recovery. Fixture native receipts are labeled synthetic; actual browser/native authority is separate evidence.
requirements.title: Verify guarded dispatch and failure behavior

acceptance_criteria.text: A browser session searches and inspects a concept, explores a relation/derivation, edits a draft, observes a validation error, reviews a diff, publishes an authorized change, and reopens its canonical result.
Separate cases verify rejected/unauthorized publication, concurrent-edit conflict, draft preservation, keyboard operation, and readable non-graph access.
A static screenshot, mockup, or frontend-only fixture does not establish end-to-end editing or publication.

requirements.assessment: Actual CUA sessions searched, inspected a derivation, edited and corrected a draft, reviewed/rejected/reopened/published exact content, and verified canonical publication. Separate actual read-only and two-tab conflict cases prove the required negative paths.
requirements.title: Verify real browser editing workflows

acceptance_criteria.text: The combined flow resolves a concept, derives a fact with provenance, uses advanced retrieval where selected, generates and reviews a proposal, and applies an authorized visual change through a semantic guard.
Representative independent solver assignments receive the same advanced packet digest; post-dispatch ontology changes follow reassessment without silent context replacement.
Before/after checks prove canonical memory preservation, project isolation, no unintended product adoption, and continued core operation with advanced profiles disabled.

Release acceptance supplies current evidence for each required capability and interface; unavailable prerequisites or unexercised integration remain incomplete rather than being replaced by a smaller demonstration.

requirements.assessment: The selected generation-native project joins sourced native generation, current concept retrieval/inference, optional embeddings and browser publication through enabled guards. Separate actual native manager/solver acceptance and exact preservation/destination reports complete the integrated evidence.
requirements.title: Validate second-release integration and preservation

verification_basis: Criterion-by-criterion host review of the actual implementation, current passing suites, scoped reviewer findings, and reopened native/browser/backend evidence. Each evidence file retains its own versions and limits.
